formation.title: The Unification of Arabia
formation.text:
After generations of tribal fragmentation, the Arabian Peninsula is united under a single banner for the first time since the early caliphates. The holy cities of Mecca and Medina, the incense ports of Yemen, the pearl-rich shores of the Gulf, and the vast Najdi interior all answer to one sovereign.

This is a moment of profound significance. The land that gave birth to Islam and served as the crossroads of ancient trade routes is whole again. But what path shall this reborn Arabia follow? Shall it raise the banner of jihad and ride forth to expand the faith by force of arms, as the first caliphs did? Or shall it look inward, cultivating the trade networks and scholarly traditions that made Arabia the envy of empires?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: Ride forth under the banner of faith!

modifiers.name: Sword of the Prophet
modifiers.text: The united Arabian state shall be forged through the sword of faith, its cavalry sweeping across the desert to bring the scattered tribes under one banner. From Mecca to the furthest oases, the call to arms shall echo.

options.text: We shall be the crossroads of the world once more.

modifiers.name: Cradle of Civilization
modifiers.text: Arabia stands at the crossroads of three continents, inheritor of the incense routes, the pilgrimage trade, and the scholarly traditions that lit the world from Baghdad to Cordoba. This legacy of commerce and learning shall be the foundation of a greater state.

advances.name: Bedouin Raiding Traditions
advances.text: The Bedouin razzia, the lightning raid across the desert, is both an art of war and a way of life, honed over centuries of tribal conflict in the Arabian wastes.

advances.name: The Incense Route
advances.text: For millennia, the wealth of southern Arabia flowed north along caravan routes carrying frankincense and myrrh from the groves of Dhofar and Hadramaut to the markets of the Mediterranean.

advances.name: Spate Irrigation
advances.text: When the rains break in the mountains, the wadis of the Tihama and the Hadramawt run for a few days. Earth and stone barrages turn the flood onto the fields, and each village takes its turn at the water by a rule older than any dynasty.

advances.name: Tribal Confederacy
advances.text: Arabian governance rests on the delicate balance of tribal alliances, where a paramount sheikh maintains authority through personal prestige, mutual obligation, and the distribution of raiding spoils.

advances.name: Pearl Diving
advances.text: The shallow waters of the Arabian Gulf yield pearls of extraordinary luster, harvested by divers who descend to the seabed with nothing but a weighted stone and leather finger guards.

advances.name: Desert Navigation
advances.text: Bedouin navigators read the desert like sailors read the sea, by the stars, the wind patterns in the sand, and subtle variations in terrain that mark the paths between distant oases.

advances.name: Dhow Shipbuilding
advances.text: The distinctive lateen-rigged dhow, with its sewn-plank hull and shallow draft, is perfectly adapted to the monsoon winds of the Indian Ocean and the shallow waters of the Gulf.

advances.name: The Hajj Economy
advances.text: Millions of pilgrims journeying to Mecca and Medina each year create a vast economic engine of caravanserais, provisioners, guides, and merchants that sustains the Hejaz.

advances.name: Qadi Courts
advances.text: The qadi, learned in Islamic jurisprudence, serves as judge in disputes both civil and criminal, providing a framework of law and order rooted in the Quran and the hadith.

advances.name: Date Palm Cultivation
advances.text:
The date palm is the tree of life in Arabia, providing food, timber, fiber for rope, and shade for other crops. Its cultivation in irrigated oases is the foundation of settled Arabian life.

Available in: Date Palm Grove

advances.name: Arabian Horse Breeding
advances.text: The purebred Arabian horse, bred for endurance, loyalty, and speed across millennia of selective care, is the most prized cavalry mount in the world. Bedouin tribes guard their mares' bloodlines as zealously as they guard their honor.

advances.name: Sufi Mysticism
advances.text: The mystical orders of Islam have deep roots in Arabia, where Sufi shaykhs lead communities in spiritual exercises, poetry, and the pursuit of divine knowledge through direct experience.

advances.name: Mocha Coffee Trade
advances.text: The port of Mocha in Yemen has become the sole gateway for the world's supply of coffee, a commodity that has spawned a global network of coffeehouses and a lucrative monopoly.

event.title: The Coffee of Mocha
event.text:
The port of Mocha on the Red Sea coast has become the center of a new and extraordinary trade. Coffee, first cultivated in the highlands of Yemen by Sufi mystics seeking to stay awake for night prayers, has captivated the tastes of the wider world. European, Indian, and Ottoman merchants crowd the harbor, their ships laden with silver and goods to exchange for sacks of dark, aromatic beans.

Coffeehouses have sprung up across Arabia and beyond, becoming centers of conversation, commerce, and political debate. The governors of Mocha grow wealthy from export duties, and the highland farmers tend their precious plants with jealous care, prohibiting the export of fertile seeds to prevent rivals from establishing their own plantations.

options.text: Mocha shall be the jewel of our trade empire.

modifiers.name: Mocha Trade Boom
modifiers.text: The port of Mocha hums with commerce as merchants from Europe, India, and Africa converge to trade in the dark aromatic beans that have captured the world's palate.

options.text: Control the plantations, control the wealth.

modifiers.name: Coffee Monopoly
modifiers.text: Strict control over the coffee plantations of the Yemeni highlands and the export facilities at Mocha creates a monopoly on the world's most fashionable commodity.

advances.name: Indian Ocean Maritime Trade
advances.text: Arabian dhows have sailed the monsoon routes for centuries, connecting the Red Sea and Persian Gulf to India, East Africa, and the spice islands of Southeast Asia.

advances.name: Imamate Governance
advances.text: The Ibadi imamate of Oman and the Zaidi imamate of Yemen represent distinctive Arabian traditions of religio-political authority, where the imam combines spiritual leadership with temporal governance.

advances.name: Desert Fortresses
advances.text: The qasr, a fortified desert stronghold of mud-brick and stone, guards the trade routes and water sources of the interior, serving as both military garrison and center of tribal authority.

advances.name: Spice Middlemen
advances.text: Arabian merchants have long served as intermediaries in the spice trade, purchasing pepper, cinnamon, and cloves from Indian and Southeast Asian producers and selling them at enormous markup to European and Ottoman buyers.

advances.name: Arabian Firearms Adoption
advances.text: The adoption of firearms by Arabian warriors transforms desert warfare, combining the mobility of mounted nomads with the devastating firepower of the matchlock musket.

advances.name: Sharifian Authority
advances.text: The Sharifs of Mecca, claiming descent from the Prophet Muhammad, wield an authority that transcends tribal boundaries, lending legitimacy to any ruler who can secure their endorsement.

advances.name: The Aden Entrepot
advances.text: The natural harbor of Aden, commanding the strait between the Red Sea and the Indian Ocean, has been a vital entrepot for maritime trade since antiquity.

advances.name: Tribal Cavalry Reform
advances.text: The traditional Bedouin raiding style is formalized into disciplined cavalry formations, retaining the desert mobility and horsemanship while adding tactical coordination and strategic purpose.

advances.name: Camel Corps
advances.text: The dromedary camel, capable of traveling vast distances without water, enables the creation of military units that can traverse terrain impassable to conventional armies.

advances.name: Wahhabi Reform Movement
advances.text: The alliance between religious reformer Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab and the House of Saud in 1744 creates a powerful religio-political movement that transforms the Arabian Peninsula.

event.title: The Wahhabi Reformation
event.text:
A religious scholar from the Najd, Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, has ignited a movement that is transforming the peninsula. Preaching a return to what he considers the pure, original practices of Islam, he denounces the veneration of saints, the elaborate rituals of Sufi orders, and what he sees as centuries of accumulated superstition and innovation.

His alliance with a local ruler has created a formidable religio-political movement. Warriors inspired by his teachings sweep through the desert, toppling shrines and demanding submission to their austere vision of the faith. The movement's energy is undeniable, but its rigid interpretation of doctrine risks alienating moderate subjects and neighboring powers alike.

How shall we respond to this upheaval of the spirit?

options.text: Embrace the purifying fire of reform.

modifiers.name: Wahhabi Zeal
modifiers.text: The austere reformist message has swept through the peninsula, purging what its adherents see as innovations and returning the faithful to the pristine practices of the earliest generations.

modifiers.name: Pragmatic Reform
modifiers.text: The impulse toward religious renewal has been tempered by political realism, creating a state that values doctrinal clarity while maintaining the diplomatic flexibility needed to govern a diverse peninsula.

advances.name: The Ikhwan Warriors
advances.text: The Ikhwan, settled Bedouin warriors dedicated to religious study and military service, combine the endurance of desert nomads with the discipline of motivated zealots.

event.title: Rise of the Ikhwan
event.text:
A new breed of warrior has emerged from the settlements of the Najdi desert. The Ikhwan, the 'Brothers,' are former Bedouin tribesmen who have abandoned their nomadic ways to settle in agricultural communities dedicated to religious study and military training.

Driven by intense religious conviction, they combine the desert endurance and riding skills of their ancestors with a fanatical discipline that makes them fearsome on the battlefield. They fight not for plunder or tribal honor, but for the glory of God and the expansion of the true faith. Their settlements, the hijra, serve as both military garrisons and centers of religious instruction.

options.text: These warriors shall be the vanguard of our destiny.

advances.name: Arabian Modernization
advances.text: Contact with Ottoman and European powers introduces new ideas of governance, technology, and education to the peninsula, spurring efforts to modernize without abandoning tradition.

advances.name: Oasis Agriculture
advances.text: Advanced irrigation techniques transform scattered oases into productive agricultural centers, supporting larger populations and providing the economic base for a centralized state.

advances.name: Pearl Trade Boom
advances.text:
The insatiable global demand for Gulf pearls has transformed coastal communities into prosperous trading centers, with pearl merchants commanding wealth that rivals that of the great caravan traders.

Available in: Pearl Diving House

advances.name: Gulf Naval Patrol
advances.text: Armed patrol ships guard the vital sea lanes of the Persian Gulf and Red Sea, protecting Arabian trade from pirates and projecting power across the maritime frontier.

advances.name: Modern Arab Army
advances.text: The creation of a standing army trained in European military methods marks the transformation of Arabia from a confederation of tribal warriors into a modern state capable of projecting centralized power.

advances.name: Arab National Awakening
advances.text: A new consciousness of shared Arab identity, rooted in common language, history, and culture, inspires a movement for political unity and self-determination across the peninsula.

advances.name: Port Modernization
advances.text: The modernization of Arabian ports with European-style docks, warehouses, and repair facilities connects the peninsula to the global economy of the industrial age.

advances.name: Desert Infrastructure
advances.text: The construction of roads and communication lines across the vast Arabian interior binds the scattered oases and tribal territories into a unified state for the first time.

advances.name: Tribal Conscription
advances.text: The traditional tribal obligation to provide warriors on demand is formalized into a conscription system, ensuring that every settlement contributes to the defense of the unified state.

advances.name: Unified Arab State
advances.text: The culmination of centuries of effort, a centralized Arabian state that has transcended tribal divisions, integrating diverse peoples under a common administration and shared identity.

destiny.name: Destiny of Arabia
destiny.text: With Arabia united, the question of its future burns bright. Shall the peninsula look outward to conquest and faith, or inward to commerce and civilization? The stability of the realm must first be secured before either path can be pursued.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: Arabia Ascendant
event.text: The peninsula is united, the tribes have sworn allegiance, and the holy cities stand under our protection. For the first time in centuries, an Arab state commands respect among the powers of the world. The question now is not whether Arabia will rise, but how high.

destiny.name: The Fertile Crescent
destiny.text: The lands of the Fertile Crescent, Damascus, seat of the Umayyads, and Baghdad, city of the Abbasids, were once the heartlands of Arab civilization. To restore the caliphate, these ancient capitals must be reclaimed, and with them Kufa, the camp city of the first conquests.

conditions.text: Chose Sword of the Prophet
Own Damascus, or a subject owns it
Own Baghdad, or a subject owns it
Own Kufa, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Crescent Reclaimed
event.text: Damascus and Baghdad, the twin jewels of Arab civilization, once again answer to an Arab sovereign. The great mosques that echoed with the decrees of caliphs past shall echo again with the authority of a renewed Arab state. The Fertile Crescent, breadbasket of empires, feeds our ambitions as it once fed the Abbasids.

options.text: The ancient capitals are ours once more.

destiny.name: Jihad of the Faithful
destiny.text: The holy city of Jerusalem and the ancient land of Egypt must be brought under the banner of the restored Arab state. With Cairo, half of Lower Egypt behind it and Jerusalem's sanctity, the caliphate's claim to lead the Muslim world becomes unassailable.

conditions.text: Own Cairo, or a subject owns it
Own Jerusalem, or a subject owns it
Prestige at least 50
At least 50% of the locations of Lower Egypt are ours

event.title: The Holy Land Secured
event.text: Jerusalem stands under our protection, and the wealth of Egypt flows into our treasury. The restored Arab state now commands both the spiritual authority of the holy places and the material resources of the Nile valley. Yet the question arises, shall we press forward with militant fervor, storming every fortress in our path? Or shall we consolidate these vast gains with garrisons and patience, letting our strength grow behind fortified walls?

modifiers.name: Militant Jihad
modifiers.text: The warriors of the caliphate storm fortifications with fanatical courage, overwhelming defenders through sheer aggression and tactical initiative.

options.text: Fortify what we hold and grow strong.

modifiers.name: Caliphal Garrison
modifiers.text: A network of fortified garrisons secures the caliphate's vast new territories, with reinforced walls and disciplined troops maintaining order across conquered lands.

destiny.name: The Caliphate Restored
destiny.text: From Aleppo to Basra, from Mosul to the desert's edge, the full extent of the original caliphate must be reunited under Arab rule, with half of the Levant held and not its cities alone. This is the ultimate ambition, a new golden age of Islamic civilization, governed from Arabia.

conditions.text: Own Aleppo, or a subject owns it
Own Basra, or a subject owns it
Own Mosul, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Caliphate Reborn
event.text:
From the shores of the Mediterranean to the headwaters of the Tigris, from the deserts of Sinai to the mountains of Kurdistan, the caliphate lives again. Not since the age of Harun al-Rashid has an Arab sovereign commanded such vast domains. The world watches as Arabia takes its place among the great empires of history.

But how shall this restored caliphate define itself? As the sword that expands the faith through force of arms? Or as the just ruler who governs diverse peoples with wisdom and wins their loyalty through fair dealing?

options.text: By the sword of God shall we prevail!

modifiers.name: Sword of Islam
modifiers.text: The caliphate's military machine operates with ruthless efficiency, sustaining campaigns across vast distances while the faithful fight with tireless dedication.

options.text: Justice and wisdom shall be our legacy.

modifiers.name: The Just Caliph
modifiers.text: The caliph governs with wisdom and fairness, winning the loyalty of diverse peoples through just administration and shrewd intelligence networks.

destiny.name: Masters of the Gulf
destiny.text: The Strait of Hormuz and the ports of Oman control the flow of trade between the Indian Ocean and the Persian Gulf. To become the crossroads of the world, Arabia must first command these vital chokepoints and accumulate the wealth they generate.

conditions.text: Chose Cradle of Civilization
Own Hormuz, or a subject owns it
Own Masqaṭ, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 1000

event.title: Masters of the Strait
event.text: The great chokepoint of Hormuz is ours, and the ancient port of Muscat stands under the Arabian flag. Every ship passing between the Indian Ocean and the Persian Gulf must now acknowledge Arabian supremacy. The wealth of India, Persia, and East Africa flows through waters we command.

options.text: The Gulf is an Arabian sea.

destiny.name: The Monsoon Routes
destiny.text: Arabian merchants have sailed the monsoon winds for millennia, and the trade they carry must now be counted and taxed. The incense that once made Arabia rich, and Jeddah, where the India fleets come in on the monsoon, must be harnessed: build up the port and raise a warehouse there where the cargoes wait for the next ship.

event.title: The Monsoon Winds
event.text:
Our merchants ride the monsoon winds from the Gulf to India and beyond, while our banks finance the trade that passes through our ports. The ancient incense routes have given way to a modern commercial network, but Arabia remains at its center.

Shall we build a navy to protect and enforce our maritime dominion by force? Or shall we focus on the institutions of trade, the banks, the exchanges, the merchant houses, that make our ports indispensable regardless of who commands the seas?

options.text: Command the seas with Arabian warships!

modifiers.name: Maritime Dominion
modifiers.text: Arabian warships enforce control over the vital sea lanes, blockading rivals and protecting the merchant fleets that carry the wealth of three continents.

options.text: Build the institutions that make us rich.

modifiers.name: Trading Empire
modifiers.text: A vast network of merchant vessels connects Arabian ports to markets across the Indian Ocean, sustained by experienced captains and favorable banking arrangements.

destiny.name: Crossroads of Continents
destiny.text: Aden commands the passage between the Red Sea and the Indian Ocean, the hinge between three continents. With the port built up into a great city, the pepper of India passing through its markets and vast wealth accumulated, Arabia can claim its ultimate destiny, not as a conqueror, but as the indispensable hub through which the world's commerce must flow.

event.title: Crossroads of the World
event.text:
Arabia stands at the intersection of three continents, and the world's trade flows through our ports. From Aden to Hormuz, from Jeddah to Muscat, Arabian merchants connect Europe with Asia and Africa with the East. Our banking houses finance ventures across oceans, and our markets set prices that echo in distant capitals.

This is the zenith of Arabian commerce. Shall we use this position to foster a new golden age of arts, learning, and diplomacy? Or shall we press our commercial advantage to its fullest, ensuring that Arabia remains the indispensable crossroads through which all trade must pass?

options.text: Usher in a new golden age!

modifiers.name: Arabian Golden Age
modifiers.text: A renaissance of arts, learning, and diplomacy radiates from the Arabian Peninsula, as the wealth of trade funds scholars, artists, and ambassadors across the known world.

options.text: We are the crossroads. The world pays us.

modifiers.name: World's Crossroads
modifiers.text: Arabia has become the indispensable nexus of global commerce, where every trade route converges and every merchant must pay tribute to the guardians of the strait.

units.name: Bedouin Raider
units.text: Lightning-fast desert cavalry raised from the tribal levies, experts in the razzia, the traditional Bedouin raiding strike that has terrorized caravans and settled peoples since time immemorial.

units.name: Camel Rider
units.text: Mounted on the hardy dromedary, these riders can traverse vast stretches of waterless desert, serving as scouts, raiders and light cavalry where no horse-mounted force can follow.

units.name: Tribal Conscript
units.text: Conscripted warriors drawn from the settled tribal communities, providing the mass infantry needed to defend the expanded Arabian state.

units.name: Arabian Musketeer
units.text: Disciplined infantry armed with matchlock muskets, trained to deliver devastating volleys before drawing their curved swords for close combat in the Arabian tradition.

units.name: Najdi Cavalry
units.text: Reformed tribal cavalry from the Najd heartland, combining traditional desert horsemanship with disciplined tactical formations. Supreme in arid and desert warfare.

units.name: Ikhwan Warrior
units.text: Fanatically devoted infantry drawn from the settled Bedouin communities, the Ikhwan fight with a fervor born of deep religious conviction, making them fearsome shock troops.

units.name: Modern Arab Infantry
units.text: Regular infantry trained in European military methods, equipped with modern weapons, and organized into disciplined formations capable of sustained campaigns.

units.name: Arabian Dhow
units.text: The iconic lateen-rigged trading vessel of the Arab world, fast and nimble in the monsoon winds, though lightly armed compared to European warships.

units.name: Indian Ocean Dhow
units.text: A larger, ocean-going variant of the traditional dhow, capable of sailing the long monsoon routes between Arabia, India, and East Africa.

units.name: Gulf Patrol Ship
units.text: An armed coastal vessel designed to patrol the shallow waters of the Persian Gulf and Red Sea, protecting trade routes from pirates and foreign interlopers.

buildings.name: Incense Warehouse
buildings.text: A fortified storehouse for the precious resins of frankincense and myrrh, the ancient wealth of southern Arabia that once flowed along caravan routes to the Mediterranean world.

buildings.name: Wadi Barrage
buildings.text: A deflector of earth and stone across the wadi bed. It turns the seasonal flood into canals and onto the fields, which are soaked once and sown at once.

buildings.name: Date Palm Grove
buildings.text: An irrigated palm garden of the oasis. Its gardeners prune the palms, pollinate the female trees by hand and keep the water channels clear, and the oasis bears more dates for the caravans and the ships.

where.text: The location's raw material is Fruit

buildings.name: Hajj Caravanserai
buildings.text: A way-station on the pilgrimage routes to Mecca, providing food, water, shelter, and trading opportunities to the endless stream of faithful making the hajj.

buildings.name: Mocha Coffeehouse
buildings.text: A gathering place where merchants, scholars, and travelers exchange news and ideas over cups of dark, aromatic coffee from the Yemeni highlands.

buildings.name: Desert Qasr
buildings.text: A fortified desert stronghold of mud-brick and stone, guarding the trade routes and water sources of the Arabian interior against raiders and invaders.

buildings.name: Entrepot Warehouse
buildings.text: A major trading warehouse in a port city, where goods from India, Africa, and Europe are stored, sorted, and resold, forming the backbone of Arabian maritime commerce.

buildings.name: Pearl Diving House
buildings.text: The house that sends out the pearling boats. It outfits the dhows, advances the divers and pullers their keep against the season's catch and buys what they bring up, and the banks off its shore yield more pearls than the boats of single families ever found.

where.text: The location's raw material is Pearls

buildings.name: Modern Port
buildings.text: A port facility equipped with modern docks, cranes, and repair yards, connecting Arabia to the steam-powered maritime trade of the industrial era.

buildings.name: Caliphal Diwan
buildings.text: The central administrative bureau of the restored caliphate, where scribes record decrees, tax registers are maintained, and the business of governing a vast empire is conducted with methodical precision.

buildings.name: Arabian Trade Exchange
buildings.text: A grand marketplace where merchants from three continents conduct business, with permanent trading halls, secure warehouses, and resident factors representing commercial interests from India to Europe.

list.name: Custodianship of the Two Holy Mosques
list.text: Founded in 1201 when Sharif Qatadah ibn Idris seized Mecca from the Banu Thaqif, the Hashemite Sharifate ruled the Hejaz under successive overlordships (Mamluk, then Ottoman after 1517) until 1925. The Sharif drew his religious legitimacy from descent of the Prophet through al-Hasan ibn Ali, and exercised practical sidana of the Kaaba and the Prophet's Mosque. Ottoman sultans styled themselves Khadim al-Haramayn al-Sharifayn after Selim I's conquest of Egypt; the surrah of gold dispatched annually from Damascus and Cairo was distributed by the Sharif's office among the resident ulema, the great waqf endowments, and the poor of the Two Sanctuaries.

conditions.text: Owns Mecca

list.name: Zaydi Imamate of Sa'da
list.text: In September 1597 al-Mansur al-Qasim, a Zaydi Sayyid of the Rassid line, proclaimed the Imamate at Sa'da against Ottoman imposition of Hanafi fiqh on the Yemeni highlands. By 1608 the Qasimid imams had recovered the highland districts and signed a ten-year truce with the Porte; by 1636 they had expelled the Ottoman garrisons of Mocha and the Tihama. The Imamate ruled through the sada (Sayyid scholar-judges claiming Hashemite descent) who dispensed Zaydi-Hadawi jurisprudence from district centres at Sa'da, Sanaa, and Shihara, summoning tribal levies by religious call rather than feudal tenure.

conditions.text: Shiism religion

list.name: Ibadhi Imamate of Nizwa
list.text: The Ibadhi Imamate of Oman, first proclaimed in 750 CE and revived in 793 and many times thereafter, was an elective theocracy. The Imam was chosen by the assembly of ulema (the ahl al-hall wa-l-aqd) and could be deposed by the same body if found wanting. The capital alternated between Nizwa and Rustaq; provincial walis were named by the Imam from among the scholarly families. The Imamate held that absolute political and military power should never rest with any one man, producing a markedly decentralised government that endured into the twentieth century alongside the coastal Sultanate of Muscat.

conditions.text: Ibadism religion

list.name: Dirah and Hima
list.text: The dirah was the customary tribal territory of the Najdi and Bedouin confederacies: not a fixed border but an elastic claim over grazing grounds, watering points, and seasonal pastures, enforced by raiding (ghazu) and shaykhly arbitration. The hima reserves set aside ground for named animals in named seasons; wells were marked, blood-debts adjudicated in the majlis, and access negotiated between shaykhs at neutral fairs. No central state could function in the Najd without binding the great confederacies (Anaiza, Shammar, Mutair, Qahtan) by subsidy or arms; settled regimes that ignored the dirah lost their revenue from the desert margins within a generation.

list.name: Mocha Customs Administration
list.text: After the Ottoman conquest of Yemen in 1538, every Red Sea ship was required by decree to put in at Mocha and pay customs there. Through the seventeenth century roughly 10,000 tonnes of beans annually moved through its warehouses, parched or roasted before export to prevent germination outside Yemen. After 1636 the Qasimid imams inherited the office of nakhuda al-bunduq and continued the Ottoman regime: a divan of three officials (the wali, the muhtasib, and the nakhuda al-bahr) assessing duties at five to ten per cent on imports and a flat tariff per bahar of coffee. European factories at Mocha (English, Dutch, French) paid the same fee structure into the eighteenth century.

conditions.text: Owns Al-Muḵā

list.name: Diriyah Pact
list.text: In 1744 (1157 AH), at the oasis town of Ad-Diriyah in Najd, Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab and the local emir Muhammad ibn Saud swore mutual bay'a: the religious scholar would direct doctrine and the dawah, the emir would provide arms and political headship. The compact created the First Saudi State (1744-1818) and a fused religio-political apparatus in which mutawwiun rode with Saudi commanders, qadis appointed by the House of al-Sheikh applied a strict Hanbali jurisprudence, and revenue was extracted as zakat from the conquered tribes. The Ikhwan brotherhoods that grew from this compact carried Wahhabi doctrine across the peninsula by the early nineteenth century.

conditions.text: Sunnism religion
Owns Ad-Dir'iyya
